newsitem.title: UK: Britain's FTSE sets record, but awaits Labor tax news.
newsitem.headline: Britain's FTSE sets record, but awaits Labor tax news.

text.p: Leading British stocks rose to set a record Friday, defying expectations of a sharp fall in reaction to Labour's massive election win, as investors opted to await government decisions on corporate and dividend taxes and interest rates.

The FTSE 100 index added 10.6 points to close at a record 4,455.6, after almost matching its 4,466.5 trading high set on April 30. The benchmark index had been expected to plunge as much as 100 points if Labour won. The FTSE hit a session low of 4,423.6 in thin early trade.
"The FTSE at these levels is saying 'The election's over now let's get back to business as usual,'" said one senior dealer at a major securities brokerage house.
"In fact, the market remains on hold, waiting to see if Labour has any ability to govern and what they are going to do on tax," he said.

Traders and analysts said the unexpectedly large victory for Labour would increase fears of higher corporate taxes in the first budget. The new government's parliamentary majority will be about 180 seats.
"They are in an unbelievable position of power and as a group they have never run the country before. We are heading for a few months of mega uncertainty," a dealer said.
But several strategists said the FTSE was as likely to react to share price movements on Wall Street over the next few days as to decisions made by the new government.

"The City feels reassured that Labour have the same macro policies as the Conservatives," said NatWest Markets UK equity strategist Bob Semple. "What we're going to face in the next few days and the next few months is concerns over tax risks," he said.
The main hurdle for the stock market was expected to be Labour's first budget and the fear that it would hit the corporate sector hard.
"If it's two months before we see a budget, it will leave the market in a very moribund state," said James Dewhurst, equity salesman at Charterhouse Tilney.
